tldr: This paper presents "RevoSim," a scalable multimodal tactile simulator that integrates visuotactile fingertips with a piezoresistive palm array, achieving up to 4,096 parallel environments on a single RTX 5090.
hero_caption: Overview of the multimodal tactile data generated by RevoSim and reinforcement learning tasks: (a) Depth, RGB, and marker displacement from fingertip sensors; (b) In-hand ball rotation using depth from all five fingers; (c) Bottle grasping combining palm pressure with fingertip depth.
overview:
In robotic dexterous manipulation, tactile feedback is essential for capturing fingertip slips and fine contact states. However, collecting data on real hardware leads to sensor wear and damage, creating a strong demand for reinforcement learning (RL) in simulation. Unfortunately, prior tactile simulators focused either purely on camera-based visuotactile sensors or solely on pressure distribution array sensors. None existed that could simulate an entire multi-fingered hand with heterogeneous tactile sensors in parallel.

To address this gap, the authors developed "RevoSim," a multimodal tactile simulator designed for the BrainCo Revo3 multi-fingered hand. The Revo3 features high-resolution visuotactile sensors on its five fingertips to capture fine deformation, alongside an array of 285 piezoresistive taxels (tactile pixels) distributed across the palm and finger pads. This study builds a framework that faithfully reproduces the responses of these two vastly different sensor modalities based on real-world calibration data, while generating them synchronously at high speed on a GPU.

In experimental evaluations, an adaptive sampling method that targets only the contact region reduced VRAM consumption for fingertip depth generation by about 70% compared to existing methods across 1,024 parallel environments. Furthermore, using a single RTX 5090, the authors demonstrated that a massive RL environment with 4,096 parallel instances can be constructed for marker displacement. They trained policies for in-hand object rotation and grasping entirely within simulation, establishing a new foundation for tactile-driven manipulation learning.
contributions: Built the first hand simulator that synchronously generates heterogeneous tactile modalities in parallel, combining visuotactile sensors across 5 fingers and a 285-taxel piezoresistive array.
Reduced VRAM consumption for depth generation by approximately 70% compared to TacMap through contact-adaptive local ray tracing, all while preserving high resolution.
Reproduced realistic physical interactions and electrical/mechanical crosstalk across taxels on curved palms and finger pads using a surface normal-aware diffusion model.
Demonstrated full-hand tactile policy learning completely inside simulation by running up to 4,096 parallel environments on a single RTX 5090.

sections.heading: Why Do We Need Whole-Hand Multimodal Tactile Simulation Right Now?
sections.summary: Dexterous manipulation requires tactile feedback to sense slipping and localized contact, but data collection on physical hardware suffers from sensor wear. Existing simulators focus on a single sensing modality and lack the capacity to rapidly simulate an entire hand with heterogeneous sensors. RevoSim was created to bridge this gap.
sections.details:
Robotic dexterous manipulation is inherently contact-dominated. While vision from external cameras and proprioception from joint encoders provide a rough picture of the scene, they cannot directly detect incipient slip (the onset of micro-slippage), moving contact points, or occluded contacts. Consequently, tactile feedback is indispensable for controlling immediate contact dynamics.

However, running reinforcement learning with tactile sensing directly on real hardware is exceptionally challenging. Collecting large amounts of data causes the delicate elastomer surfaces of tactile sensors to wear out or tear. Furthermore, tactile data is high-dimensional and heavily hardware-dependent, spurring a pressing need for fast, sim-to-real-ready simulators.

Existing tactile simulators include impressive work: some render fingertip camera images or marker motions, others solve elastic deformation, and some employ approximations to achieve high throughput for RL. There are also simulators dedicated to distributed pressure arrays. Yet, most handle only a single sensor family or simple planar taxel grids. Accurately modeling diverse, non-uniform sensors distributed across an entire hand while sustaining the throughput needed for massive parallel RL remained unachieved.

RevoSim fills this void. The target BrainCo Revo3 hand combines optical visuotactile fingertips with piezoresistive arrays on the palm and phalanges. RevoSim integrates both modalities while accounting for real-world geometry, sensitivity, hysteresis, and electrical/mechanical crosstalk, enabling fully synchronized simulation across parallel environments.

sections.heading: Simulating Multimodal Tactile Signals with Speed and Physical Realism
sections.summary: RevoSim models 11 pressure regions and 5 visuotactile fingertips on the Revo3. It applies a normal-aware curved diffusion model for piezoresistive taxels and introduces an adaptive ray-tracing scheme that automatically tracks contact regions with coarse-to-fine sampling to drastically lower computational costs.
sections.details:
### II-A System Overview
At each simulation step, RevoSim synchronously generates the whole-hand pressure vector $\mathbf{p}_{t} \in \mathbb{R}_{+}^{285}$, five fingertip depth images $\mathbf{D}_{t} \in \mathbb{R}_{+}^{5\times 240\times 320}$, corresponding RGB images $\mathbf{I}_{t}$, and 3D displacements for 100 calibrated markers per fingertip $\mathbf{M}_{t} \in \mathbb{R}^{5\times 100\times 3}$ directly on the GPU.

### II-B Geometry-Aware Pressure Simulation
The piezoresistive taxels across the palm and finger pads each have a position $\mathbf{x}_{i}$ and an outward normal $\mathbf{n}_{i}$. First, the penetration depth $d_{i,t}$ and velocity $\dot{d}_{i,t}$ are computed from the object's signed distance field (SDF). Baseline pressure is then calculated using calibrated parameters, including stiffness $k_i$, damping $c_i$, sensitivity gain $g_i$, and saturation force $F_i$.

A key innovation here is a curvature-aware diffusion kernel. If pressure is simply diffused using 3D Euclidean distance, forces leak to opposite surfaces with opposing normals, such as the back of a finger. To prevent this, RevoSim uses a tangent plane projection matrix $\mathbf{P}_i = \mathbf{I} - \mathbf{n}_i\mathbf{n}_i^\top$ to define a symmetric distance metric $D_{ij}$ that incorporates the inner product of surface normals. This diffuses pressure in a geometrically consistent direction while conserving the total response, successfully recreating hardware-specific crosstalk.

### II-C Adaptive Visuotactile Simulation
Each fingertip has a nominal $240\times 320$ ray grid. Performing collision checks across all pixels every step would be computationally prohibitive. RevoSim therefore adopts a two-stage approach.

First, a coarse $32\times 24$ grid checks for contact to isolate a region of interest (ROI) where contact actually occurs. Next, rays are cast inside this ROI using a fixed $25\times 40$ grid to determine accurate penetration depths. Finally, bilinear interpolation reconstructs the full $240\times 320$ dense depth image. By fixing the total number of ray queries while tracking contact locations, RevoSim decouples output resolution from computational cost and achieves dramatic speedups.

### II-D RGB Image and Marker Displacement Synthesis
The reconstructed depth is converted into RGB images using a GPU-accelerated Taxim pipeline. It composites contact residuals onto a pre-captured zero-contact background image, preserving the sensor's optical characteristics.

For marker displacements, the framework decouples elastomer surface dilation from temporal shear deformation. An expansive dilation field derived from normal penetration is combined with a hydroelastic shear state based on contact motion history. These fields are then sampled at 100 calibrated marker locations and fed directly as policy observation features.

sections.heading: Achieving 4,096 Parallel Instances on a Single GPU: Real-World Comparisons and Policy Learning
sections.summary: Using an RTX 5090, memory efficiency and scaling were measured: RevoSim reduced depth VRAM by ~70% compared to TacMap at 1,024 environments and achieved up to 4,096 environments with marker displacements. Sensor outputs qualitatively matched physical hardware, and policies for ball rotation and bottle grasping were successfully trained in simulation.
sections.details:
### III-A Experimental Setup and Baselines
The pipeline was built on Ubuntu 24.04 using Isaac Lab 2.3.2 and evaluated on an NVIDIA RTX 5090. Visuotactile simulators TacMap, TacSL, FOTS, and HydroShear were used as baselines to evaluate peak process VRAM and maximum parallel environments.

### III-B Computational Scalability
- **Memory Footprint for Depth and Deformation**: When generating depth-only across 1,024 environments, RevoSim consumed only 9.2 GiB of VRAM compared to TacMap's 30.6 GiB, achieving an approximate 70% reduction. This highlights the effectiveness of the adaptive sampler keeping query counts constant.
- **Deformation Scaling**: In the depth-conditioned marker displacement configuration, RevoSim scaled up to 4,096 parallel environments within a 31.36 GiB VRAM envelope. In contrast, FOTS and HydroShear crashed with out-of-memory (OOM) errors at this scale, and TacSL topped out at 256 environments.
- **Modality Ablation**: Adding pressure on top of depth introduced virtually zero overhead. Adding marker displacements or RGB images increased memory consumption, capping the maximum capacity at 1,024 environments when all modalities were enabled. This flexibility allows users to pick modalities based on their needs.

### III-C Qualitative Comparison with Real Sensors
The fidelity of the simulation was compared against physical sensors. In the visuotactile fingertips, local elastomer depression and radial/shear marker displacements closely matched optical tracking from the real sensor. For the piezoresistive sensors, pressing a spherical object produced a smooth, normal-dependent pressure diffusion from the contact center to neighboring taxels, consistent with readouts from the physical hand's index pad.

### III-D Tactile Reinforcement Learning Tasks
Two manipulation policies were trained in RevoSim. The first was "in-hand ball rotation" using depth from all five fingertips. The second was "bottle grasping" combining fingertip depth with the palm pressure array. The palm array provided crucial feedback for contacts occluded from fingertip cameras, demonstrating that stable whole-hand tactile policies can be learned entirely within simulation.

sections.heading: Summary and Future Directions
sections.summary: RevoSim successfully bridges visuotactile and piezoresistive sensing with outstanding memory efficiency, supporting up to 4,096 parallel environments. Future work includes expanding sensor compatibility, simulating deformable objects, incorporating richer temporal dynamics, and validating sim-to-real policy transfer.
sections.details:
RevoSim provides a scalable and high-fidelity platform capable of jointly simulating 285 piezoresistive taxels and five visuotactile fingertips on the Revo3 hand.

By coupling a curvature-aware pressure diffusion model with an adaptive contact-tracking sampler, the framework slashes depth VRAM by 70% and achieves unprecedented scalability—running 4,096 parallel environments on a single modern RTX 5090. This makes full-hand multimodal tactile RL computationally practical.

For future work, the authors plan to support additional sensor types, model soft deformable objects, incorporate more detailed temporal dynamics, and systematically validate sim-to-real transfer of policies trained inside the simulator onto physical robots.

takeaways: Combining visuotactile sensing (local geometry/deformation) and pressure arrays (whole-hand load distribution) covers fingertip camera blind spots, enabling coordinated grasping.
Decoupling contact detection via a coarse grid from detailed ray casting in a targeted ROI drastically cuts ray-tracing overhead without sacrificing image resolution.
Using a surface normal-aware distance metric for pressure diffusion prevents physically implausible force leakage across thin structures, such as between the front and back of a finger.
Enabling 4,096 parallel tactile RL instances on a single GPU massively accelerates training efficiency for contact-rich dexterous manipulation.
limitations: Physical sim-to-real transfer of policies learned in the simulator is not demonstrated in this paper and remains future work.
Enabling all modalities simultaneously (depth + markers + RGB + pressure) increases memory consumption, capping parallelism at around 1,024 environments.
Simulation is currently focused on rigid body contacts and has not yet been extended to deformable, soft-object manipulation.
